Who shot the Sheriff?

By: Joy Summers | Commission

Proposal


Show: Carte Blanche

One Liner (Tonight on Carte Blanche...):
Sheriffs are the enforcement arm of the courts. Without them the justice system would cease to operate. But what if this vital arm of the justice system has been captured, by the very people who are s

Unique Selling Point:
Case studies willing to go on camera, damning emails, an affidavit from a driver revealing bank account details and amounts of payments for positions, and a former deputy minister prepared

Summary:
Sheriffs are the enforcement arm of the courts. Without them the justice system would cease to operate. But what if this vital arm of the justice system has been captured, by the very people who are supposed to ensure its smooth functioning.
What if a shadow syndicate, allegedly run by its own "Mr. Clean" Chairperson, has captured the board, turning a vital arm of the justice system into a cash-for-jobs franchise. We reveal a story that is chilling as a board member is gunned down, the driver reveals all, but later retracts and is promoted to a deputy sheriff by the very board member he has made allegations against, and Sheriffs who have served the public faithfully over many years are pushed out.



Further information:
Act I: The Illusion and the Exodus
• The "Mr. Clean" Facade: We introduce Mark Morgan. He has political cover at the highest level. He is an acting judge, and has taken over the mandate to oversee sheriffs.
The Breaking Point: We reveal the frustration of former Deputy Minister of Justice, John Jeffrey. It is not the Board’s job to select sheriffs—that is the Ministry's mandate. Jeffrey saw the overreach, the hijacking of the appointment process, and the lack of transparency. Ultimately, he resigned in disgust, leaving Morgan dug in, unchallenged, and fully in control of the board.
Act II: The Syndicate and the Price of a Badge
With the Ministry out of the way, we expose the mechanics of the corruption.
• The Franchise Model: This isn't just mismanagement; it’s a highly organized syndicate. We explain how Morgan is illegally franchising acting sheriff positions and outright selling permanent, highly lucrative positions.
• The Whistleblowers: We introduce our on-the-ground case studies—legitimate sheriffs pushed out, intimidated, and replaced by unqualified individuals who simply bought a license to print money.
• The Smoking Gun: We bring in the affidavit from Morgan’s former driver, Lucky. This is the ultimate insider betrayal. He details acting as the bagman, picking up illicit cash and depositing it into bank accounts belonging to the sheriffs buying their posts.
Act III: The Dead Man and the Ledger
We follow the money, proving that the board's own finances are being weaponized.
• The Numbers Don't Lie: We present our forensic accountant’s breakdown of the 2023/2024 and 2024/2025 annual reports. The numbers simply do not make sense.
• The Fidelity Fund Raid: The fund meant to protect the public has been raided to finance its own regulator. Unclaimed trust funds are reclassified. Fortunes are blown on opaque travel and security while financial controls collapse.
• The Terrified Accountant: We reveal the trail of panicked emails from the former accountant. They sent these warnings to one man: Board Member Andrew Tshabalala.
• The Assassination: Andrew questioned Morgan. He had the emails. He saw the numbers. Just as he was preparing to go public, he was murdered.
The Russian Playbook
We end on a chilling geopolitical twist that elevates the threat level.
• The Bizarre Alliance: With the domestic board captured and the funds bleeding dry, Morgan is looking overseas. But not to democratic allies—he is aligning the South African Sheriffs with the Russian Bailiffs Society.
• The Final Question: Why? What can an authoritarian state's enforcers teach South African sheriffs? It paints a terrifying picture of the future of the profession if this syndicate is not dismantled.

Audio

Voice over 1
They have trust funds often holding millions of Rands.

Each operates in a particular geographical area, and while they run their businesses privately, they’re answerable to the Justice Ministry.

Their job is to serve legal papers, and confiscate and auction assets where court orders have been handed down.

These are the sheriffs of the court.

Link
It’s not easy to understand how sheriffs work but there are only two things you need to understand: number 1, sheriffs are the enforcement arm of the courts and number 2 these positions are very lucrative, and everyone wants a slice of the action.

VO 2
We’ve investigated startling allegations made by whistleblowers: that sheriff positions are up for sale.

Up sound Mark Morgan
It gives me great pleasure today to address you…

This is Mark Morgan.

Viewed as a rising star by some, he’s already an acting judge despite being relatively young.

He is also chairperson of the Board for Sheriffs, responsible for regulating the profession.

Iqbal Mohammed
And here comes Mr. Morgan, now newly appointed, and says that all of this shenanigans is going to come to an end. And we look at this man and say, "Here's the saviour."




Page 2

VO3
Morgan promised to remove rotten sheriffs who steal public money, but he is now accused of selling sheriff positions.


Seboka
It was a rampage! It was a real rampage!

VO4
Since he took over, questions have been raised around how money from a public Fund, managed by the board for sheriffs, is being spent.

Iqbal Dawood Mahomed
These funds, especially fidelity funds, are sacrosanct.
Lourensa
You can't touch that money.
Iqubal
You can't touch it. You can’t touch it.

Up sound Marching
Left right! Left right!

VO 5
Mark Morgan, seen here signing an agreement with counterparts from Russia’s Federal Bailiff Service, has bodyguards, and a penchant for international travel.

Up sound Right, left!

His critics say he’s attempting to militarize how local sheriffs operate.

Thaka Seboka
There is a lot of fear within the profession. I bet you if you were to go to any other sheriff, they will not even give you a hearing, because they are afraid to be seen.
VO 6
There were indeed people too nervous to talk to us. But those who were willing to go on record made deeply troubling claims about a vital part of our judicial system.

FADE TO BLACK HERE page 3

VO 7
In April last year, a former board member and sheriff called Andrew “Oupa” Shabalala was murdered.

Although there’s no evidence that Morgan was involved, sources tell us Shabalala was about to publicly expose him.

Lourensa
Were you afraid at that point?
Iqbal
I'll still say I'm afraid up to this point, to here.

NEW VO 8
Advocate and former sheriff, Iqbal Mohammad, knew Shabala and was deeply shocked by his murder. But he remains one of the few prepared to go on camera.

Iqubal
It’s very important for the public to understand what is happening. Because if this persists, It's going to undermine our entire judiciary. The sheriff is a vital cog in this whole system.

Up sound exterior and then to interior

Lourensa
So back in the day, how big were your offices?
Seboka
I employed about 20 people.

VO 9
Before retiring, Thaka Seboka spent almost 20 years as an attorney and sheriff.

Sheriffs earn commission on documents served and assets auctioned. In Seboka’s office, gross income could reach over R100 000 in a single day.

Lourensa
This specific region, Pretoria Central would have been the jewel in the crown?
Seboka
Certainly. This was one of the best lucrative offices in the country.

VO 10
Serving on the Board for Sheriffs, Seboka was well respected. When it came time for him to retire, he says Morgan - who he claims, wanted to sell his practice to the highest bidder - tried to push him out early.


Thaka
So, it baffled me when he said that there were complaints against my office, which up to today have not been proved.
Lourensa
Is your suspicion then that money was exchanged for these decisions?
Thaka Seboka
Certainly. It's a real reality that has been proven, where money has exchanged hands.

VO 11
Several court battles ensued, but ultimately Morgan approached the Justice Ministry, which had the power to remove Seboka. And, just like that, he was out.


VO 12
In April last year, he put his concerns in a letter to the new Justice Minister, Mmamaloko Kubayi, sending it to her direct email address.

Seboka
And sadly, the Minister gave my documents, the concerns that I gave to her, to Morgan himself.
Lourensa
But that's outrageous.
Thaka
Well I was surprised and embarrassed and, you know, also confused…
Lourensa
Because essentially you are acting as a whistleblower.
Thaka
Of course, yes.
Lourensa
And she's exposing you to the person you are blowing the whistle on. That’s dangerous.

Thaka
Yes, exceptionally dangerous. But I took the decision then that these things have got to come out in the open.
Lourensa
What did Morgan then say after all of this?
Thaka
Well, to my surprise, Morgan called me and said to me, the minister has given me your documents.

VO 13
Kubayi has recently introduced a new bill aimed at protecting whistleblowers, making it an offence to reveal their identities.

Presenter
If you were to be approached by a whistleblower making complaints about the chairperson of the board how would you handle that?
Minister: I would act. I receive whistleblower information daily. I act.
Presenter:
Our understanding is that Mr. Taka Seboka did contact you with whistleblower information.
Minister: No Never.
Presenter:
Let me just finish the question, and he made these complaints. He put it on paper, and he put it to you, Minister.
Minister:
No, don't put it as a fact. It's not a fact.
Presenter: And that same… well, this is what he states, so we have to put this to you, minister. His suspicion is that that information somehow got relayed to Advocate Mark Morgan. So we have a whistleblower approaching the minister about Advocate Mark Morgan and in that same week he's contacted by Advocate Morgan. How did that information reach him?
Minister: Okay. Let's take it back.
Lourensa
How did that information reach him?
Minister
Let's take back and don't make allegations that are unsubstantiated.
Presenter: I'm just putting these claims to you, Minister.
Minister: Eh Eh. In the email I've asked you for evidence of it being sent to me, I don't have.
Presenter: He contends that he received this from you, Minister. Good morning Ntate Seboka…

VO 14
We shared Seboka’s email and the response he says he got from the Minister on WhatsApp.

Lourensa: …apologise for not indicating action taken. Was that not your response?
Minister: No, I don't remember that.
Presenter: Okay.
Minister: I'll have to check that.
Okay.
Minister:
I don’t remember Mr Seboka at all.
Lourensa:
Okay, you don’t remember him?
Minister:
No.

VO 15
But Seboka wasn’t the only sheriff battling Morgan.

Mahomed, who practiced as a sheriff for 29 years, shares Seboka’s view that Morgan has been secretly selling off sheriff appointments to the highest bidder.

It’s a view echoed by other sheriffs we spoke to, who don’t appear on camera.

Lourensa
How soon into Advocate Morgan's tenure did you realise that he wasn't the saviour you thought he was?
Iqbal
About less than a year, within less than a year.

VO 15
Oupa Shabalala was under investigation before he was murdered. But he sent Mahomed a string of emails.

Iqbal
Somewhere along the way, things between Oupa and Mr. Morgan fell foul.

In them, board members claimed Morgan was a rogue chairman making decisions on his own. They also alleged Morgan was benefiting from serious financial misconduct.

Money due to members of the public is held in a sheriff’s trust account until payment. If that money is stolen, victims are able to claim from something called the Fidelity Fund. It’s a type of insurance policy managed by the Board for Sheriffs.

Iqubal Dawood Mahomed
His own board members pointed out that there's 55 million rand missing from the Fidelity Fund.
Lourensa
That's a lot of money.
Iqbal
That's a lot of money.

Link
The uneasy feeling within the profession was soon confirmed by this explosive affidavit from Advocate Mark Morgan’s driver. Cash, he alleged, was indeed changing hands, and he attached the receipts to prove it.

VO 16
This is the driver in question, Lucky Mashaba. According to several sources, he drew up an affidavit in January last year. He gave a copy to Mohammed.

Lourensa
Was he emotional? Was he angry?
No. He seemed very cool and calm.

VO 17
The affidavit includes these stamped bank receipts covering a period of seven months. They show cash deposits made to a company of which Morgan is a director, and to another owned by a politically connected businesswoman.

Iqbal
It shows, for example, on the 20th of February, 2023, there's an amount of R500,000 rand received.
Lourensa
What is the total amount that Mr. Mashaba alleges he had to pay or deposit into these bank accounts?
Iqbal
There's an amount of R1,082,826.
Lourensa
Does Mr. Lucky Mashaba allege that he was asked to deposit these sums of money into different bank accounts?
Iqubal
Yes,he was instructed by Mr. Morgan.
Lourensa
Why would advocate Mark Morgan do this? What's in it for him?
Iqbal
Money. I believe it's purely a question of money.

VO18
Are the cash deposits, the payments sources say Morgan is taking, in exchange for lucrative, sought-after sheriff posts?

Then, inexplicably, three months later, Mashaba retracted his affidavit.

Link
Advocate Mark Morgan declined our request for an interview, instead suggesting we refer any allegations to law enforcement agencies.

VO19
In a detailed written response, he later denied all wrongdoing.

After a brief absence as board chair, Morgan was reappointed by Minister Kubayi on the recommendation of her department.

Minister Kubayi
That's one. Number two, I have not received any substantive complaint against him as a minister.
Lourensa
Minister I just want to mention this to you, we have an affidavit made by the former driver for Advocate Mark Morgan, Lucky Mashaba. Now he contends that he was used to ferry money around, big deposits of cash.
Minister: Have you seen this one?
Presenter:
What is this one?
Minister:
It's an affidavit from him that says that that affidavit is actually fraudulent.
Presenter: Why does he contend it was fraudulent?
Minister: I don't know.

VO 20
But we’re not convinced. The retraction affidavit was signed just three days after Tshabalala was gunned down.

And why was the minister so determined not to acknowledge the deposits to Morgan’s company, listed in the original affidavit?

Lourensa
Well, we've spoken to another source that says on the day that Mr. Mashaba made this affidavit….
Minister Kubayi
I am not an investigator
Lourensa
There's no reason to believe that on the day that he made these claims… And I mean, we can go through this. He added bank statements and receipts. If it was fraudulent, how would he have been able to manufacture these receipts?
Minister Kubayi
The question you should be asking is from the police.
Lourensa
Well, we’ll certainly ask that question, Minister…
Minister:
And then say to the police, "Police, there are two affidavits with damning affidavits with all this with a case number with a person opening fraud, what have you done?"

VO 21
But, by law, the Minister is compelled to report any reasonable suspicion of corruption in excess of R100 000.

After Shabalala’s murder, Mashaba disappeared - but recently Mahomed managed to speak to him on the phone.

Iqubal Dawood Mahomed
Ten minutes after that, I get a call from Mr. Morgan. And he referred very specifically to Lucky. Is there anything about Lucky that you need to discuss with me?

VO 22
We tried to speak to Mashaba ourselves, but he didn’t answer our messages.

The Minister insists she’s had no complaints against Morgan. But Carte Blanche has evidence - including a detailed report from the Law Society - to contradict her claim.

Presenter
So just to be clear, Minister, you are saying from where you are sitting, everything regarding advocate Mark Morgan and the way he is acting as the chairperson of the board is above board.
Minister:
Above board.
Lourensa
Okay.

VO 23
Seboka isn’t convinced.

Thaka
I have no doubt that there is corruption. I strongly believe there's corruption and it is deep seated.


VO 24
As important questions linger, between them, Seboka and Mohammed have asked the police, parliament and other law enforcement agencies to investigate.

Lou
Do you feel like you're fighting a losing battle?
Iqbal
I hope not. I hope the public out there is paying attention, is going to put in its claims. And this money should not be abused. So I hope that something will come out of this.

THE END





PROMO ONE

VO
Serious allegations emerge from inside the sheriff’s profession

Thaka Seboka
I strongly believe there's corruption and it is deep seated.
VO
But the justice minister says - nothing to see here
Minister Kubayi
That affidavit is actually fraudulent
Lourensa
How would he have been able to manufacture these receipts
Minister
The question you should be asking is from the police.

PROMO TWO

Positions for sale, financial irregularities, nervous whistleblowers – the South African board for sheriffs under the spotlight
Lourensa
Were you afraid at that point?
Iqbal
I'll still say I'm afraid. If this persists, It's going to undermine our entire judiciary. The sheriff is a vital cog in the whole system.

PROMO THREE

LINK
This is a story about the SABFS, doesn’t sound that interesting right? But dig beneath the surface and it sounds like a movie

Iqbal
And we look at this man and say, "Here's the saviour."
Left right left right
Minister
Dont make allegations that are unsubstantiated
Lourensa
I am just putting claims
Minister
Eh eh you are not putting claims

metadata.Summary: Sheriffs are the enforcement arm of the courts. Without them the justice system would cease to operate. But what if this vital arm of the justice system has been captured, by the very people who are supposed to ensure its smooth functioning. What if a shadow syndicate, allegedly run by its own "Mr. Clean" Chairperson, has captured the board, turning a vital arm of the justice system into a cash-for-jobs franchise. We reveal a story that is chilling as a board member is gunned down, the driver reveals all, but later retracts and is promoted to a deputy sheriff by the very board member he has made allegations against, and Sheriffs who have served the public faithfully over many years are pushed out.
metadata.Further information: Act I: The Illusion and the Exodus • The "Mr. Clean" Facade: We introduce Mark Morgan. He has political cover at the highest level. He is an acting judge, and has taken over the mandate to oversee sheriffs. The Breaking Point: We reveal the frustration of former Deputy Minister of Justice, John Jeffrey. It is not the Board’s job to select sheriffs—that is the Ministry's mandate. Jeffrey saw the overreach, the hijacking of the appointment process, and the lack of transparency. Ultimately, he resigned in disgust, leaving Morgan dug in, unchallenged, and fully in control of the board. Act II: The Syndicate and the Price of a Badge With the Ministry out of the way, we expose the mechanics of the corruption. • The Franchise Model: This isn't just mismanagement; it’s a highly organized syndicate. We explain how Morgan is illegally franchising acting sheriff positions and outright selling permanent, highly lucrative positions. • The Whistleblowers: We introduce our on-the-ground case studies—legitimate sheriffs pushed out, intimidated, and replaced by unqualified individuals who simply bought a license to print money. • The Smoking Gun: We bring in the affidavit from Morgan’s former driver, Lucky. This is the ultimate insider betrayal. He details acting as the bagman, picking up illicit cash and depositing it into bank accounts belonging to the sheriffs buying their posts. Act III: The Dead Man and the Ledger We follow the money, proving that the board's own finances are being weaponized. • The Numbers Don't Lie: We present our forensic accountant’s breakdown of the 2023/2024 and 2024/2025 annual reports. The numbers simply do not make sense. • The Fidelity Fund Raid: The fund meant to protect the public has been raided to finance its own regulator. Unclaimed trust funds are reclassified. Fortunes are blown on opaque travel and security while financial controls collapse. • The Terrified Accountant: We reveal the trail of panicked emails from the former accountant. They sent these warnings to one man: Board Member Andrew Tshabalala. • The Assassination: Andrew questioned Morgan. He had the emails. He saw the numbers. Just as he was preparing to go public, he was murdered. The Russian Playbook We end on a chilling geopolitical twist that elevates the threat level. • The Bizarre Alliance: With the domestic board captured and the funds bleeding dry, Morgan is looking overseas. But not to democratic allies—he is aligning the South African Sheriffs with the Russian Bailiffs Society. • The Final Question: Why? What can an authoritarian state's enforcers teach South African sheriffs? It paints a terrifying picture of the future of the profession if this syndicate is not dismantled.
